newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't hits out at labor decree challenge.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't hits out at labor decree challenge.

text.p: The Argentine government Friday slammed a court ruling that declares its labor reform decrees unconstitutional and vowed to appeal it, get the judge disqualified, and possibly seek his impeachment.
"It's a ridiculous ruling...more political and ideological than judicial," Social Security Secretary Carlos Torres told a news conference after the weekly cabinet meeting.

"The government will seek the annulment of the ruling, the disqualification of the judge and of course if impeachment is in order, we'll seek it in Congress," he said, arguing on the technicality that Judge Julio Garcia Martinez's court was not even supposed to be open Thursday, a court holiday.
President Carlos Menem's Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez told local radio the ruling was "plagued with irregularities" and the "decrees ruled by the executive will remain in place."

Judge Garcia Martinez's ruling said the decrees ruled by Menem in December "have transgressed, modified and violated article 14 of the national constitution," which guarantees union coordination of collective wage talks.

The decrees allow workers to choose their union health plan, permit smaller firms to bypass national unions in collective wage talks and let employers appeal to the government if they want to negotiate with unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.

The government was planning to sign three more decrees in coming weeks to push ahead with further labor reforms. It opted for presidential decrees in the face of opposition in Congress and a breakdown in negotiations with unions.
The main CGT union federation staged a 24-hour strike on December 26, its third in the year, to demonstrate against the decrees. Unions fear the reforms will weaken their power.
GCT chief Rodolfo Daer told reporters his union had also petitioned to have the decrees annulled as unconstitutional and would seek the support of the International Labor Organization.

Opposition Radical Party Congress leader Federico Storani defended Judge Garcia Martinez's challenge, saying: "It's not a political ruling but one that is in line with the law, because these decrees affect workers' acquired rights."
